title: The Modes
intro: Start the major scale's pattern of steps from a different note and you get a mode. The seven modes share one set of notes but each has its own tonic and its own character, from bright Lydian to dark Locrian.

blocks.text: Play only white keys but treat a different note as home and you hear each mode. Each differs from the major scale on the same tonic in one or more degrees:

items: Ionian (C to C): the major scale.
Dorian (D to D): minor with a raised 6th. Bright for a minor mode; 'So What', 'Scarborough Fair', much funk.
Phrygian (E to E): minor with a lowered 2nd. Dark and Spanish-sounding; flamenco and metal.
Lydian (F to F): major with a raised 4th. Dreamy, floating; film scores, 'The Simpsons' theme.
Mixolydian (G to G): major with a lowered 7th. Rock and blues ('Norwegian Wood', 'Sweet Child o' Mine' verses).
Aeolian (A to A): the natural minor scale.
Locrian (B to B): minor with lowered 2nd and 5th. Its tonic triad is diminished, so it is rarely a home key.

blocks.text: Ordered from brightest to darkest, each mode lowers one more degree: Lydian, Ionian, Mixolydian, Dorian, Aeolian, Phrygian, Locrian. Seen on C: Lydian has F♯; Ionian none; Mixolydian B♭; Dorian adds E♭; Aeolian adds A♭; Phrygian adds D♭; Locrian adds G♭.

widget.title: All seven modes on C (same tonic, so you hear the colour)

blocks.text: Finding a mode on any note

Two ways work. Parent scale: D Dorian uses the notes of C major because D is 2̂ of C, so E♭ Dorian uses the notes of D♭ major (E♭ is 2̂ of D♭). Alteration: take the major or minor scale on the tonic and apply the characteristic change, so E♭ Dorian is E♭ natural minor (E♭ F G♭ A♭ B♭ C♭ D♭) with a raised 6th: C instead of C♭.

Medieval church modes (Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, with plagal forms) organised plainchant by final note and range. Ionian and Aeolian were added by Glarean in 1547. The major–minor system of 1600–1900 grew out of them. The modern use of modes as colours over a drone or a vamp comes from folk music, modal jazz (Miles Davis's Kind of Blue, 1959) and rock.

Hold a drone in the left hand (the tonic, or tonic and fifth) and improvise with the white keys in the right hand. A drone on D makes everything Dorian; on E, Phrygian; on F, Lydian. This is the fastest way to hear what each mode's characteristic note does.

blocks.title: Parent scales
blocks.text: Which major scale contains the notes of A Mixolydian? Of F♯ Phrygian?
solution: Mixolydian is the mode on 5̂, so A Mixolydian is the 5th mode of D major (A is 5̂ of D).
Phrygian is the mode on 3̂, so F♯ Phrygian is the 3rd mode of D major too (F♯ is 3̂ of D).

blocks.title: Spell a mode
solution: G major is G A B C D E F♯; Lydian raises 4̂, so C becomes C♯: G A B C♯ D E F♯ G. (It is the 4th mode of D major.)
blocks.answer: G A B C♯ D E F♯ G
